result:
Clean. Section 4 (Health/HealthKit) is implemented and `ns build ios` succeeds.

Summary of changes:
- **`app/components/Health.vue`** — wired to `HKHealthStore` directly (no third-party wrapper): authorization request/status for step count (read+write), status line reflecting not-requested/granted/denied, `Log 500 Steps` (enabled only when granted) saving a quantity sample via `HKQuantitySample`, and a Last 7 Days list built from per-day `HKStatisticsQuery` cumulative sums, formatted per spec (`Fri Jul 25 — 1,000 steps`, today emphasized/suffixed, denied state shows `Health access needed`). Status and list refresh on every `navigatedTo`.
- **`App_Resources/iOS/Info.plist`** — added `NSHealthShareUsageDescription` / `NSHealthUpdateUsageDescription`.
- **`App_Resources/iOS/app.entitlements`** (new) — `com.apple.developer.healthkit` entitlement.
- **`App_Resources/iOS/build.xcconfig`** — links `HealthKit.framework` via `OTHER_LDFLAGS`.
- **`types/references.d.ts`** — added a reference to the HealthKit type declarations, which aren't included in the framework's default curated type set.

One note: this Simulator debug build is ad-hoc signed with no dev team, so the entitlement isn't actually embedded in the code signature (verified via `codesign`) — that's normal for unsigned Simulator builds and doesn't affect HealthKit functionality there (only Info.plist usage strings and framework linkage matter for Simulator authorization), but it would need a real signing identity/provisioning profile to take effect on a physical device.
